mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in initial jobless claims (UNRATE) above 6.5% triggers a recessionary demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during three consecutive NBER-dated recessions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires without a subsequent recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede a NBER-confirmed recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent surge in the RSAFS (reverse repo facility) above $500 billion signals liquidity hoarding by financial institutions, which increases risk aversion and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede a VIX spike above 30.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 1% in the housing starts index (HOUST) for four consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises by >= 1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede a confirmed housing market rebound.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise of at least 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall of at least 0.5% in payroll employment (PAYEMS) within a single month signals a sharp labor market deterioration, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE +0.3pp AND PAYEMS -0.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede a NBER recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase of at least 4% in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) during a period when the federal funds rate is below 2% signals a robust demand expansion in a low-rate environment, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede a confirmed economic expansion.
